scenario: AITA for shutting down conversation about babies? | Recently, my good friend (let’s call her B) was in town visiting and we went out for drinks at a fancy new bar with another friend of hers (let’s call her M), who I’d only met once before. We were on our first drink and having a great time, catching up on all sorts of things about our lives. Then, M started talking about someone she knows and the fertility struggles that she’s having, saying things about her “geriatric eggs” and how risky it all is at her age. Then, M grew wistful about how it was probably too late for her to have babies. For context, I’m older than any of them and have badly wanted a child for years, and fear it’s too late for me, which makes me super sad. B knows this. I said something abrupt like “this subject isn’t a good one for me” and tried to shift the subject to B’s new life in the town she moved to. I could see that B looked concerned and M was upset, so I then said something like, “Did I offend you? That wasn’t my intention.” At this point, M was tearful, and said she was trying to open up and didn’t like being told to “shut up” and was going home because I made her very uncomfortable, and stormed off. B went with her to settle the tab and make sure M found a Lyft, and then came back. Am I an ass? It was my only chance to catch up with my friend and I wanted to keep the mood light, but the evening was ruined.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was wrong or not in that situation. Let me start by going through what happened step by step. First, I was out with my friend B and another friend M. We were all having a good time, catching up. Then M started talking about someone she knows who's going through fertility struggles. She mentioned geriatric eggs and how risky it is at her age. I know that M is older than me, and I'm already in a situation where I've wanted a child for years but feel like it's too late. This makes me really sad, and B knows that. So when M started talking about this, I felt really triggered. I said something abrupt like, "This subject isn't a good one for me," and tried to shift the conversation to B's new life in the town she moved to. I could see that B looked concerned, and M was upset. Then I asked if I offended her, and she said she was trying to open up and didn't like being told to shut up. She got tearful and stormed off, saying she was going home because I made her uncomfortable. B went with her to settle the tab and make sure she found a Lyft, then came back. Now I'm wondering if I was a "nass" (which I think is slang for "nervous" or "upset") and if I was wrong in how I handled the situation. I wanted to keep the mood light because it was my only chance to catch up with my friend, but the evening got ruined. So, was I wrong to shut down the conversation? Let me think about this. On one hand, I was feeling triggered because the topic hit close to home for me. I have my own struggles with wanting a child and feeling like it's too late. It's understandable that I might want to avoid a conversation that brings up those feelings. I tried to shift the topic to something else, which is a common way to handle uncomfortable situations. On the other hand, M was trying to open up about her feelings. She was sharing something personal, and when I shut it down, it made her feel like I didn't want to hear her. She got upset and left, which is a strong reaction. It's possible that I came across as dismissive or rude, even if that wasn't my intention. I also need to consider the dynamics of the group. B was there, and she looked concerned. Maybe she noticed that M was opening up and that I was reacting negatively. It's possible that my abrupt change of subject made M feel like her feelings weren't important, which led to her being upset. I wonder if there was a better way to handle the situation. Instead of abruptly changing the subject, maybe I could have acknowledged M's feelings and expressed my own without shutting down the conversation. For example, I could have said something like, "I understand this is a tough topic, and it's something I've thought about a lot too. I'm sorry you're going through this." That way, I'm validating her feelings and sharing my own without making her feel like she's being told to shut up. Another thing to consider is the setting. We were at a bar, which is a social environment, and I wanted to keep the mood light. However, when someone brings up a serious topic, it's important to respect their need to talk about it. Trying to keep the mood light might have been at the expense of M's feelings, which isn't fair. I also need to think about how my actions affected the group. M left upset, and B had to go with her, which probably made B feel bad too. It's possible that B felt caught in the middle, which isn't a good feeling for anyone. By shutting down the conversation, I might have caused more harm than good. In the end, I want to maintain good relationships with both B and M. If I come across as dismissive or rude, it could damage those relationships. It's important to balance my own feelings with the feelings of others, especially in a social setting. So, reflecting on all this, I think I was wrong to shut down the conversation so abruptly. While I had valid reasons for feeling triggered, I could have handled it in a way that was more considerate of M's feelings. By not acknowledging her emotions and instead shifting the topic, I made her feel dismissed, which led to her being upset and leaving. It's a tough situation, but being more empathetic and open might have been a better approach.
